dossier.public_summary: The dip does not repeat at the same depth: odd and even dips differ by almost a factor of two and individual transits range from 217 to 1423 ppm, with the shallow one 6 sigma below the mean. A planet would be steady; this is the flat-bottomed echo of a stellar binary, best explained at twice the listed 13.1-day period, with a likely spot-induced secondary-like signal.

reasons.why: Odd and even eclipses differ by 691.4 ppm (depth_odd_ppm 1423 vs depth_even_ppm 731.5, depth_ratio 1.9, diff_sigma 4.492), inconsistent with a single-period planet at P=13.1 d and as expected for an eclipsing binary folded at half its true period 26.2 d.

Depth changes dramatically between sectors: 1238+/-87, 931+/-109, 217+/-106 ppm. sector_depths_by_source confirms changes_within_product (SPOC 2-min depths 1238 and 931 differ with p_constant 0.027715) and sector-level transit_depths p_consistent 9.673e-15 rejects a consistent depth even on individual transits.

Single-transit depths are inconsistent: one transit is 1423 ppm (+4.1 sigma, epoch -29 BTJD 1669.126), two deeper ~1000 ppm transits, and one much shallower 217 ppm (-6.4 sigma, epoch 84 BTJD 3150.025). This matches a source with varying eclipse depths, not a planet, despite xgboost planet_rank 0.05.
